result:
I've written the plan for w137 and marked it DONE. The three questions the last plan stopped on are settled by the answers you recorded on 2026-10-25, so nothing is left open.

All four requirements (r70, r80, r71, r83) fail today at their first step. No step writes a capability-proposal that has questions and answers. `work run` only looks at work-items, and the queue refuses to move anything to `approved` or `formulated`.

What the plan decides:
- **When apply starts:** only for a proposal that is `awaiting-answer` and has an answer for every question. A proposal with no questions at all counts as fully answered, so its apply round starts (your Q2 answer).
- **How a round runs:** each apply or formulate round is its own `initiative-round` session, started the same way as every other worker. A round "ends" when it leaves a result file `work run` can read.
- **Where a round's commits go:** when a round ends, `work run` merges its branch into the initiative branch and deletes it, before moving the proposal on (your Q1 answer). This merge has no scenario or suite check; that check only applies to an implementer finishing a work-item.
- **A round that fails:** the proposal keeps its status, `work run` exits with an error naming the round and what went wrong, and the next run starts the round again (your Q3 answer).
- **One run does it all:** apply and formulate happen in a single `work run`. Each move is committed and pushed: first to `approved`, then to `formulated`.
- **Statuses:** the queue accepts a status only if it belongs to that kind of item, so a proposal can now be `approved` and `formulated`. `work show` is unchanged and still prints nothing about proposals.

The round logic goes in a new module, `scripts/supervise_rounds.py`, with a new row in `CLAUDE.md`'s module map. Because of your answers, `scripts/supervise_merge.py` (Q1) and `scripts/supervise_faults.py` (Q3) are now in the file set too. The plan expects no existing test to break; I checked the tests the research found by searching, since there is no coverage map.

Five cases are left for the implementer to report on, not decide. Two are new with your answers:
- what happens if merging a round's branch conflicts with the initiative branch;
- what to do with a branch left behind by a failed round when the next run starts that round again.

Files are in `.shop/scratch/4-plan/`:
- plan.md
- result.json
